_comment: A frozen export, for tests only. Never a build input.
test_workflow_snapshot.py used to read db/fixtures/demo.json. That file is
regenerated from whichever business the live cluster holds, so its contents
are not a fact about the code -- and every honest export broke the suite:
once when the tenant changed name, and again when a fresh tenant exported
with zero finds and IndexError'd four tests at finds[0].
Captured 2026-08-02 from the Asaka tenant: 5 finds, 13 agent runs, one
analyst run carrying a trace. Chosen because it exercises the shapes the
operator view depends on -- decisions, artifacts, token counts, a run
receipt -- not because those numbers matter.

finds.title: Add a bookable table link so tourists can reserve
finds.summary: Nearby restaurants all appear with a 'Reserve a table' button in the lists visitors browse and Asaka does not — adding online booking puts you in front of planners.
finds.rationale: The discovery lists stored in memory show the peninsula and South Bay competitive set — Mar'sel, Sushi Inaba, bashi, Nelson's, catalina kitchen — appearing with 'Reserve a table' actions attached (dac1d463, 739e48a3, 845bbb01, 92889364). Asaka shows up in area roundups (2ab1ab9b, 4d9c6729) but with no booking path, so a visitor planning dinner from a hotel room has to phone and will often just tap the rival with a button. Your customers include visitors and tourists, who plan ahead more than locals do. A free or low-cost reservation link (Google 'Reserve with' via a booking partner, or a simple form) captures group and family bookings you currently never hear about, and gives you names and phone numbers for follow-up.
finds.move:
Pick one booking tool and sign up — OpenTable, Yelp Reservations or a free Google-integrated option.
Load your real service hours and table count into it.
Connect the booking link to your Google Business Profile 'Reserve a table' field.
Add the same link as a button on the homepage of asakakaiyo.com.
Tell staff to log walk-in wait times so you can see whether bookings smooth the peak.
Review booked covers and no-show rate after one month before deciding to keep the tool.

finds.title: Sell the ocean-view patio in your listings and photos
finds.summary: Guests rave about your patio and ocean view, but your listing description just says 'Come in and enjoy!' — lead with the view and add patio photos to win view-seeking visitors.
finds.rationale: Reviews in memory consistently name the view as the reason people remember Asaka: a million-dollar Pacific view from the patio with an ocean breeze and fair prices (b6fcd4e6), 'excellent food, reasonable price, breathtaking ocean view' (81cda6c5), 'phenomenal view, staff very friendly, great sushi, beautiful views' (0c54b40d, 7de4fc28), and 'the view is spectacular, the experience relaxed' (7301e010). Yet the restaurant description carried on your ordering listing is the generic 'Come in and enjoy!' (d1cd9215). Tourists and families searching the peninsula are choosing on scenery, and the crowded field of view-led rivals nearby means the asset you already own is invisible in text and thumbnails. Rewriting the description and leading with patio/sunset photography is free and directly targets the visitor segment you say you serve.
finds.move:
Take six clear photos on a clear afternoon: the patio with ocean behind, a sushi plate with the view in frame, and one at golden hour.
Set the best patio-with-ocean shot as the cover photo on Google, Yelp and your website.
Rewrite the Google and Yelp description to open with ocean-view patio dining and fresh sushi, then mention family and group seating.
Add 'outdoor seating' and 'scenic view' attributes on your Google Business Profile if they are not ticked.
Ask servers to invite happy patio guests to mention the view in a review.
Check Google Business Profile views and direction requests after four weeks.

finds.title: Restore online ordering via your Toast page
finds.summary: Your own site tells online customers to phone instead of ordering, while a commission-free Toast ordering page for Asaka already exists — link the two and recover those orders.
finds.rationale: Observation fd130a75 captures a banner on your menu site reading that online ordering is temporarily unavailable and asking customers to call (310) 377-5999. Meanwhile d1cd9215 shows a live Toast page for 'Asaka Japanese Cuisine, 31208 Palos Verdes Drive West' with the full food menu and the note that Toast orders are commission free and go directly to the restaurant. Online and delivery are two of your four stated discovery channels, and 0bdd2bd2 shows Asaka listed on aggregator pickup/delivery pages, so people are actively looking for a way to order. Every visitor who hits the 'call us' message on a phone at 7pm is a lost ticket — sushi is a high-ticket takeout category (fd130a75 lists $20–$39 signature plates), so even a handful of recovered orders a day is real money. This is a wiring fix, not a new product.
finds.move:
Open your website menu page and confirm the 'online ordering temporarily not available' banner is still showing.
Log into your Toast account and check that the menu, prices and pickup times there are current.
Replace the banner with a prominent 'Order Pickup' button that links straight to the Toast ordering page.
Add the same Toast ordering link to your Google Business Profile 'Order online' field and your Yelp page.
Post the ordering link once on your social accounts so regulars know it is back.
Track Toast order count weekly for three weeks against the phone-order volume you see now.

finds.title: Fix mismatched hours, name and address on every listing
finds.summary: Your closing time, restaurant name and even street address differ across Google, your site and the delivery apps — one clean-up recovers evening orders you're losing to "closed"…
finds.rationale: Four separate records of your own business disagree. Your website states takeout until 8:30pm Mon–Thu and 8:45pm Fri–Sun (221589a1). A delivery platform shows you closing at 8:00pm, with different Friday and Saturday times (0971880c). A directory listing says open daily 11:30am to 9:30pm and puts you on Palos Verdes Drive NORTH rather than West (ccf089a4). The name also shifts between "Asaka Sushi & Grill", "Asaka Sushi" and "Asaka Japanese Cuisine" across aggregators (0bdd2bd2, 0971880c, 41c46b63). Two costs follow. First, a hungry customer checking at 8:10pm on the wrong source sees you shut and orders elsewhere — and one checking against the 9:30pm listing arrives to a closed door and leaves a bad review. Second, search engines and apps treat inconsistent name/address/phone records as different or unreliable businesses, which suppresses how often you surface in "sushi near me" — the exact moment the visitor and family traffic you serve is deciding. This is entirely inside your control, costs nothing but an hour of admin, and is the cheapest demand you will find. Do this before spending on anything promotional, because ad clicks land on these same broken listings.
finds.move:
Write down your true open and close times for each day of the week, dine-in and takeout separately if they differ.
Pick one official business name and use that exact spelling everywhere.
Update the Google Business Profile with the correct name, hours, and the Palos Verdes Drive West address.
Correct the hours on asakakaiyo.com so they match.
Update hours and name on each delivery app you use, including the Friday and Saturday times.
Search your own name and phone number and fix any directory still showing Palos Verdes Drive North.
Add special hours in Google for any upcoming holiday closures.
Re-check all listings in three weeks in case an app reverted them.

finds.title: Sell the $155–$165 party platters as a bookable summer catering offer
finds.rationale: Asaka already has two high-ticket group items on its own ordering menu — a $155 Party Platter and $165 Nigiri platter (0971880c) — and the delivery listings describe the restaurant as "Group Friendly" with pickup and delivery already live (41c46b63, 0bdd2bd2). But the website's own front page pushes only generic "order online / view menu" messaging for individual sushi and never surfaces the platters (221589a1), so the highest-margin, highest-ticket product in the business is effectively invisible to the local-resident and family audience the owner wants more of. This is a demand move that costs nothing but a menu-merchandising change and a few posts: one extra platter a week is roughly $160 of revenue that the kitchen can absorb on existing prep. It is also the one category where the Terranea resort restaurants nearby do not compete — they sell in-house dining with a view, not takeaway platters for a birthday, graduation, or family gathering at home. Conservatively I am only assuming about one incremental platter per week plus a small side-order lift, not a catering business.
finds.move: With owner approval, merchandise the group platters as a named, pre-orderable product: (1) add a "Party Platters — feed 8–12, from $155" block at the top of asakakaiyo.com above the current generic order button, with a photo of each platter and a clear "order 24 hours ahead, pickup or delivery" line; (2) add both platters as items with photos and prices to the Google Business Profile menu/products section, plus one weekly Google post for the next 4 weeks aimed at local gatherings; (3) mirror the same two platters at the top of the Uber Eats / online-order listing so they are not buried below rolls; (4) put a one-line card in every takeout bag: "Hosting? Party platters from $155 — call 310-377-5999, 24 hours notice." Log every platter order and how the customer heard about it for 30 days.
